name: Jungang Market and the Downtown
tagline: The town centre around the market, where the food is
description: Sokcho's compact downtown built around Jungang market, which is the town's real institution: dakgangjeong fried chicken, squid sundae and the fish stalls. Buses to Seoraksan and the express terminal are close, and everything a visitor needs sits within a few blocks.
bestFor: Anyone who wants the market, the buses and the restaurants on foot
pros: Jungang market and the town's best food
Buses to Seoraksan and the intercity terminal
The widest accommodation choice in town
cons: Busy with visitors in the autumn foliage season

name: Abai Village and the Port
tagline: The refugee settlement across the channel, reached by hand-pulled ferry
description: A spit of land across the harbour channel settled by refugees from north of the current border who expected to go home and never did, still reached by a small ferry that passengers pull across on a cable. Low houses, fish restaurants and a distinct history.
bestFor: Stays that want the town's most distinctive quarter and the harbour
pros: The hand-pulled ferry and a genuinely unusual history
Fish restaurants and the working harbour
Five minutes across the water to the centre

name: Sokcho Beach and Daepo
tagline: The sand north and the fish market south
description: The coastal strip either side of town: a long sand beach immediately north of the harbour, and Daepo port to the south with its raw fish market where you choose the fish and eat it upstairs. Accommodation faces the sea at rents below the downtown.
bestFor: Stays that want the sea in view and the fish market a short ride away
pros: Long sand beach and East Sea views
Daepo raw fish market to the south
cons: Ten to fifteen minutes from the market and buses
Cold and very windy in winter
Crowded in the July and August beach season

name: Seorak-dong
tagline: At the national park gate, under the granite peaks
description: The settlement at the main entrance to Seoraksan, with hotels, restaurants and the cable car station, sitting directly beneath the granite walls. It is the base for anyone whose reason to be in Sokcho is the mountain, and it fills completely in the foliage weeks.
bestFor: Stays where the mountain is the whole point
pros: The park entrance and the cable car at the door
Trails to Ulsanbawi and Daecheongbong from here
cons: Twenty to twenty-five minutes into town by bus
Extremely crowded in the autumn foliage season
Resort pricing and little else to do

name: Joyang and the Residential South
tagline: The apartment districts south of the lagoon
description: The residential areas around Cheongchoho lagoon and south towards the expressway, with Korean apartment complexes, supermarkets, schools and a settled local population. Rents are the lowest in Sokcho and the lagoon path is a good running route.
bestFor: Longer stays where the rent matters more than the view
pros: The lowest rents in the town
Lagoon path for running and cycling
cons: Fifteen minutes from the market and the beach
Nothing to walk to in the evening
